query:
If deep-sea divers ascend too rapidly from ocean depths, the decreasing pressure causes nitrogen to be released as gas bubbles in the blood. This condition is known as the bends.  Sea snakes, who, like humans, breathe air that contributes nitrogen to the blood, are nevertheless able to make extremely rapid ascents and descents in ocean waters without suffering from the bends.

Sea snakes, unlike humans, can excrete nitrogen from their blood into the sea by means of extremely small blood vessels beneath their skin contributes most to an explanation of the difference described between humans and sea snakes.

repl_history.response:
The Global Context Preview mentions that "Sea snakes... can excrete nitrogen from their blood into the sea by means of extremely small blood vessels beneath their skin".

This directly explains why sea snakes don't get the bends when making rapid ascents and descents.

FINAL ANSWER: Excretion
